solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Priestess, northern mother with child endlessly

indicators.note: without an end, the word for a child loses its final letter

blocks.note: mam is a northern English dialect word for mother
a child, here a male one

explanation.surface: A list of a household: a priestess, a mother from the north and her child.
explanation.walkthrough: MAM is how a mother is addressed in the north of England; BOY loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mambo is a voodoo priestess in Haitian religion, an encyclopedic sense of the word.

clue.text: Removing spikes at the start can make you run poorly

indicators.note: only the opening letter of spikes is taken
the letters can be made into something else, a reworking of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of spikes

explanation.surface: Taking the spikes off your shoes at the start of a race will make you run badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The athletic picture hides a political answer: 'run' means govern.
explanation.definitionFit: To misgovern is to administer a country badly, and to run a state is to govern it.

clue.text: Slightly damp Oxonian at first seen in fog

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Oxonian is used
something seen inside another is placed within it

blocks.note: first letter of Oxonian
mist is a light fog

explanation.surface: An Oxford student emerges a little damp from the fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means a little wet, a near synonym of slightly damp.

clue.text: Grate temperature rising in fire causes flare-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from bottom to top
the reversed pair sits inside the word for fire

blocks.note: to grate is to rub against a rough surface
T is the abbreviation for temperature
to fire someone is to oust them from a job

explanation.surface: Heat building up in a fireplace grate causes the fire to flare.
explanation.walkthrough: The fireplace picture misleads: grate is a verb, and fire means sack.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst is a sudden eruption of feeling or activity, much like a flare-up.

clue.text: East German should stop immoral deception

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one word sits inside the other like a stopper

blocks.note: impure means morally tainted
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: An East German citizen is urged to put an end to something immoral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person; it means the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposture is the act of passing oneself off as someone else, a kind of deception.

clue.text: Unemployed daughters visiting Réunion?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so the letter sits within the word

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter(s)
Réunion is a French island, an île in French

explanation.surface: Jobless daughters take a trip to the Indian Ocean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that Réunion is an example of an island, here in its French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean out of work, with nothing to do, as workers laid off are idle.

clue.text: One missile-launcher that should get the pulse going

definitions.text: One missile-launcher that should get the pulse going

blocks.clueFragment: missile-launcher that should get the pulse going
blocks.note: surface reading: a thrilling weapon that sets the heart racing
setter's reading: pulse means legumes, so a toy that sends dried legumes flying

explanation.walkthrough: Pulse suggests a heartbeat; it is the legume family, and the toy fires those small seeds through a tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's toy tube used to blow small dried seeds at targets launches pulses as missiles.

clue.text: Elastic pressure in fluctuating pulse

indicators.note: something fluctuating keeps changing, so the letters change their order
the pressure letter is placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
the letters of pulse rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor notes stretchy blood vessels and pressure in an irregular pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means flexible and bending easily, much the same as elastic.

clue.text: Guardsman occasionally seen with officer in star gathering

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of Guardsman
a major is an army officer

explanation.surface: A guardsman is sometimes spotted with his officer at a party full of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star gathering' suggests celebrities; it means a group of stars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major, the Great Bear, is a constellation, a cluster of stars named as one.

clue.text: Small space in church given up for Welshman?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A little room in a church is surrendered for a Welsh visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Evans is a very common Welsh surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Evans is a typically Welsh surname, so a man named Evans is likely a Welshman.

clue.text: Sea monster in time one hiding argosy's last trace

indicators.note: the last of argosy's letters is the only one wanted
one thing hiding another covers it up and takes its place in the word
the first part of the clue is placed inside the sea monster's name

blocks.note: Scylla, the monster facing Charybdis in the Odyssey
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
Roman numeral one
final letter of argosy

explanation.surface: A sea monster in classical times swallows all but a trace of a great merchant ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Scylla was the monster facing Charybdis in the Odyssey; an argosy is a large merchant ship, and only its final letter matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny amount or spark, so it means a mere trace of something.

clue.text: Military title remains in old man's possession

indicators.note: something held in a person's possession is enclosed by them

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A dead soldier's rank and remains are kept by his elderly father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasha was a title of high rank given to Ottoman officers and governors.

clue.text: Line on map Charlie ignored travelling from place to place

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so the Charlie letter is dropped

blocks.note: a contour line joins points of equal height on a map
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller disregards the map lines while wandering from place to place.
explanation.definitionFit: A band or company on tour is travelling around giving performances in different towns.

clue.text: Accordingly limits sudden fear, having excised right brain part

indicators.note: excised means cut out, and right is R, so that letter goes
the first word limits, or bounds, the second on both sides

blocks.note: thus means therefore, accordingly
alarm is a sudden fright

explanation.surface: A surgeon removes part of the brain to curb sudden panic attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accordingly' is the outer word, split around the fear once that word has lost its right.
explanation.definitionFit: The thalamus is a structure deep in the brain that relays sensory signals.

clue.text: With no means to pay, second book entry incorrect

indicators.note: incorrect means wrongly set out, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the letters of book entry rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant spots a wrong entry in the books and cannot pay up.
explanation.walkthrough: Stony-broke is British slang for completely penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stony-broke means having no money at all, so one has no means to pay.

clue.text: Pixie, not so daft, provides detailed account

indicators.note: daft means silly, so these letters are muddled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: A pixie, not as silly as you think, gives a full account of events.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a comprehensive explanation or description of a subject.

clue.text: "Abundant" means the lot, regularly found in addition

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
found in means sitting inside, so the selected letters go within the last piece

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of means the lot
plus means in addition

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry: abundant means having everything, with plenty more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' looks like the link between definition and wordplay, but its letters start the alternate run.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenteous is a literary word for plentiful, existing in great quantity.

clue.text: Open to an extent, Indian prince in comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a raja is an Indian prince or king

explanation.surface: An Indian prince makes a comeback and things are opening up a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open, open only to a limited degree.

clue.text: Ways to get round man obstructed by posh Maoists?

indicators.note: to get round something is to surround it
an obstruction stands in the middle of the way

blocks.note: Rds is the abbreviation for roads
Edgar, a man's name
U means upper-class

explanation.surface: Roads are built to bypass a man blocked by snobs.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two insertions: posh goes into the man, and the ways go round the result. U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Guards were the young militants mobilised by Mao Zedong in the Cultural Revolution.

clue.text: Gentle exercise taken with Alps's top climber

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: sweet means mild, gentle
PE is physical education
first letter of Alps

explanation.surface: A mountaineer reaches the top of the Alps after some gentle exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it means a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a fragrant annual plant that climbs by tendrils.

clue.text: Creator of dynamite has book coming out for Xmas

indicators.note: coming out means leaving, so the book letter departs from the name

blocks.note: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: The inventor of dynamite publishes a book in time for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, as in carols and cards.

clue.text: Criminals' life and death situation?

blocks.note: first meaning: the realm of organized crime
second meaning: the mythical place where the dead go

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a life-or-death crisis, but it splits into two meanings of one word. The question mark flags the playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the gangland world of crime and Hades, the abode of the dead.

clue.text: Launch fitting with a different side indicator?

indicators.note: one side marker is swapped for its opposite

blocks.note: proper means suitable, fitting
L for left replaces R for right

explanation.surface: A boat launch needs the right fittings and a different light on its side.
explanation.walkthrough: Right and left are the side indicators; the R at the end of PROPER becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel is to drive or push forward, so a launch is a propelling.

clue.text: Bishop buzzing with energy in gown

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
athrob means throbbing, pulsing with excitement
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: An energetic bishop bustles about in his vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a loose dressing gown worn before or after bathing.

clue.text: Old airman drained double in pub

indicators.note: drained of its contents, only the outer shell of the word is left
the kept letters are placed inside the pub

blocks.note: first and last letters of double
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A veteran pilot downs a double measure in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Bader was a famous RAF fighter pilot of the Second World War who flew with artificial legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bader was a celebrated RAF airman, now long dead, so an old airman.

clue.text: Irish author's devotee seen in Romanian capital

indicators.note: something seen inside another is placed within it

blocks.note: the leu is Romania's currency, its capital in the money sense
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: An admirer of an Irish writer turns up in Bucharest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romanian capital' suggests Bucharest; capital here means money, and the leu is Romania's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan Le Fanu was a nineteenth-century Irish writer of gothic and ghost stories.

clue.text: What you might see on the Avon, or location on the Nile

definitions.text: What you might see on the Avon

blocks.clueFragment: What you might see on the Avon
blocks.note: first meaning, split into two words: a single white water bird
second meaning: an Egyptian city famous for its dam

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits into two words, an article and a bird; the Avon is an English river famous for swans at Stratford.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswan is a city in southern Egypt beside the Nile, site of the High Dam.

clue.text: "Shut up", author initially told

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the first letter counts

blocks.note: to pen is to write, so a pen stands for a writer
first letter of told

explanation.surface: An author is told to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pent, as in pent-up, means confined or shut in.

clue.text: Doctor round surgery to wilt from tiredness

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
O is round in shape
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A doctor doing rounds and surgery begins to flag with exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or flag, as a weary person or a thirsty plant does.

clue.text: Defeat, or we prove to be beaten

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are whisked, the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: A team must win, or show that they can be beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpower an opponent is to overcome them by superior strength.

clue.text: Irrepressible soldiers I found in noiseless setting

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within another
a setting holds a jewel all round, so the other word surrounds the letter

blocks.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers
noiseless means making no sound
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bold soldiers, and the speaker, keep going in a hushed place.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resilient bounces back from setbacks, so they cannot be kept down.

clue.text: Virgin martyr takes engagement rings back

indicators.note: to ring something is to surround it, so the letters lie inside the phrase
back means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: letters inside the phrase across the word gap

explanation.surface: A saintly young woman gets betrothed and gives back the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Agnes of Rome was a young virgin martyred for her faith in the fourth century.
